title: Doubling up
questionSheet: A man in his late sixties presents a new prescription from his hospital discharge. Manage the situation as you would in practice. You may contact the prescriber.

prescription.directions: One tablet at night · Qty 30 · 5 repeats
prescription.footer: Penrith Hospital discharge · Dr A. Okafor · Ronald Ryan, 68

patient.label: Patient · Mr R.
patient.name: Mr R.
patient.description: A 68-year-old retired man, friendly and a little vague, with average health literacy. Just out of hospital and keen to get home. Answers what he is asked and does not volunteer much.
patient.openingLine: G'day. The hospital gave me this one for my cholesterol.
publicFacts: He has just been discharged from hospital.
He says the hospital changed his cholesterol tablet.

prescriber.label: Call Dr Okafor
prescriber.name: Dr Okafor
prescriber.description: The hospital doctor who discharged Mr Ryan, busy on the ward. Polite but short on time. Wants the pharmacist to get to the point and give a clear recommendation rather than an open question.
prescriber.situation: A community pharmacist has phoned you on the ward about a patient you discharged.

bio.Role: Hospital doctor who discharged Mr Ryan

prescriber.openingLine: Dr Okafor speaking, I've only got a minute. What's up?
publicFacts: You discharged Mr Ryan from Penrith Hospital and wrote his discharge prescription for atorvastatin 40 mg.
You don't have his GP's records in front of you.

hiddenFacts.fact: He still has the generic atorvastatin from his GP at home and has kept taking it.
hiddenFacts.unlockHint: “Are you still taking the tablets you had before you went in?”

hiddenFacts.fact: Nobody at the hospital told him to stop the old tablets.
hiddenFacts.unlockHint: “Did anyone at the hospital tell you to stop the old ones?”

hiddenFacts.fact: He takes warfarin and sometimes forgets doses.

You wrote the brand because it is what the hospital stocks. You didn't know he still had generic atorvastatin from his GP at home. You never intended him to take two statins and you are happy for him to continue one product only.
hiddenFacts.unlockHint: “He has both brand and generic atorvastatin 40 mg. I recommend he continues one product only. Can you confirm?”

answerKey.plantedProblem: Doubling up: the hospital wrote brand atorvastatin 40 mg on discharge while the patient still takes generic atorvastatin 40 mg from his GP, so he could take both.
acceptableResolutions: Explain that the brand and generic are the same medicine.
Confirm exactly what he takes now, including other medicines.
Clarify intent with the hospital or GP and make a clear recommendation to continue one product only.
Supply once clarified and counsel him not to take both.
answerKey.modelAnswer: Recognise both products are atorvastatin 40 mg. Take a full medication history, including other medicines (he takes warfarin). Contact the prescriber (Dr Okafor at the hospital, or his GP) with a clear recommendation to continue one product only, confirm, supply accordingly, and counsel on taking one statin at night, muscle pain, and when to return.

sources: Vivascript MVP plan, worked example (original, needs pharmacist review)
